title: Strip slash-command markup from titles
description:
42 conversations (1.4%) show garbage as their result header — harness-injected markup
reaching the title verbatim instead of the prose the user actually typed. Examples:
`find-skills` from a slash-command expansion, a sentence about whichever file happened to be
focused in the editor, and bracketed interruption notices the harness writes as though the
user had typed them.

Both importer paths are affected and they need different rules, because the two tools inject
differently: Claude Code wraps machinery in pseudo-XML tags, Codex writes bare slash-command
lines and `[$name](path)` skill links.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `cs index`
2. `cs search` with a blank query to list recent conversations, or search for `find-skills`.
3. Scan the grouped result headers. 42 of them are markup rather than prose — a
   slash-command expansion, an `ide_opened_file` sentence, or `[Request interrupted by user]`.

Blocks the eval set (chat-search-6eb.9): a result header that shows machinery makes
"is this the conversation I meant" unanswerable, so relevance judgements would be scored
against a title the ranking never saw.
acceptance_criteria: No conversation title on either the claude-code or codex path contains harness-injected markup. A turn that is entirely markup yields no title and the next user message gets the job. <command-args> keeps its body when the sibling <command-name> is a custom command and yields nothing when it is /model or /fast. Bare bracketed harness notices never title a conversation. Codex bare slash-command lines are rejected while real paths (/Users/x, /usr/local/bin) and prose containing a slash are not. All 42 affected conversations render real prose. Synthetic tests only.
close_reason: Verified against a fresh full-corpus index: 0 conversation titles contain pseudo-XML markup, ide_* blocks, bracketed harness notices, or bare slash commands. Both importer paths covered by synthetic tests.

title: ymd() renders dates in UTC, so evening-local conversations show tomorrow date
description:
A session at 2026-07-18 21:00 PDT prints as 2026-07-19. Every grouped result line is
affected, and a wrong date makes "is this the one I meant" unanswerable.

Not a rare edge: `ymd()` renders in UTC, so on Pacific time every conversation after 17:00
local shows tomorrow's date — roughly seven hours of every day, and the evening is when a
lot of this corpus was written.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Find a conversation whose `ended_at` is an evening local time — 2026-07-18 21:00 PDT is
   2026-07-19 04:00 UTC.
2. `cs index`, then `cs search` for it.
3. The grouped result header reads 2026-07-19. It should read 2026-07-18.
design:
DECIDED: take chrono, convert to local at the parse boundary, keep storage as epoch millis.

Rationale from fast-resume (the category leader, already benchmarked against): it depends on chrono 0.4 and uses Local exclusively — Utc appears nowhere in its src/. Adapters convert at parse time (adapters/shared.rs parse_datetime returns DateTime<Local> via with_timezone(&Local), with a naive-local fallback for offset-less formats), then reduce to f64 epoch seconds for storage. Local-ness is a render/bucket concern, never a storage one — which matches ended_at already being epoch millis here.

Rejected: reading TZ or /etc/localtime for a fixed offset. Correct for ymd() today, wrong the moment date arithmetic appears. fast-resume's next_day_start_seconds uses checked_add_days(Days::new(1)) — civil-day arithmetic — and its test proves a next-day boundary is 82,800s across spring-forward and 90,000s across fall-back, neither of which a fixed offset can express. chat-search-6eb.11 (Query DSL) would want exactly this for after:/before:/yesterday filters.

Testing note: fast-resume keeps chrono-tz as a DEV-dependency only, to pin a zone (Europe/Paris) so DST behaviour is deterministic in tests. Production reads the system zone. Worth copying.

The old localtime_r advisory does not apply — chrono 0.4 has not pulled in time 0.1 by default for years.
acceptance_criteria: Dates render as the local civil date: a conversation at 2026-07-18 21:00 PDT prints 2026-07-18. Storage stays epoch millis — local-ness is a render concern, never a storage one. A test pins the behaviour against a fixed zone via chrono-tz as a dev-dependency only, so it is deterministic in CI regardless of the runner's zone. The rule lives in exactly one place, landing as part of chat-search-me9.12 rather than separately, so ymd() in the binary and the strflocaltime call in the cs-fzf jq both go away.
close_reason: Landed as part of me9.12. cs-core/src/time.rs owns the rule; DST behaviour pinned with chrono-tz as a dev-dependency; Group.ended_date rendered in cs-core so no client re-derives it.

title: ChatGPT reaches the index only via --chatgpt-export
description:
69% of the corpus vanishes silently if the flag is omitted. An eval run without it measures
the wrong index and nothing says so.

The ChatGPT export is the only source not read through `ArchiveReader` — `crates/cs/src/query.rs:63-79`
reads it straight from a directory handed in on the command line, which is why it is the one
source that can be forgotten.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `cs index` with no flags.
2. `cs search` for a phrase you know is in a ChatGPT conversation.
3. Zero hits. The run reports success and its per-source table simply has no
   `chatgpt-export` row — nothing states that 2,011 conversations were not considered.
4. `cs index --chatgpt-export ~/dev/sandbox/chat-history/data/`, search again, and the same
   phrase is found.
acceptance_criteria: ChatGPT conversations are indexed on a default run with no extra flags, or the run refuses to proceed and says what is missing.
close_reason: chatgpt-export is now an ordinary mirror source in config.toml and the --chatgpt-export flag is gone; a bare 'cs index' reaches all 2,011 ChatGPT conversations. Also closes the silent half of the acceptance: a configured source the archive holds nothing for now gets a report row stating why (bundle-not-implemented vs nothing-archived) instead of being skipped invisibly — opencode now shows as skipped rather than absent.

title: Should the fts tables carry a prefix index? It is most of what a broad keystroke costs
description:
fts5 answers a prefix term by scanning its term index for every term with that prefix and merging their doclists, and it redoes that on every query. On the 180k-message corpus that is the dominant cost of a broad typeahead keystroke, measured two independent ways while doing chat-search-6eb.30:

- Ranking (search_grouped, limit 50, nested 0): `pro` 29.4 ms, `the` 59.3 ms, against `commit` 5.2 ms and `borrow` 0.5 ms. Same shape chat-search-6eb.29 measured as `rus` 1193 ms / `rust` 25 ms.
- Marking one row through the corpus index: `the` exact 54.6 us/row against `the`* 5427 us/row — 100x, on the same rows, differing only in the star.

A prefix index (`prefix='2 3 4'` on the CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE) turns those into ordinary single-term doclist lookups for the configured lengths. Prefixes longer than the longest configured length fall back to the scan, so the choice of lengths is the whole decision.

## What has to be decided

Which prefix lengths, if any, against how much index growth. Each configured length is another full posting list over the corpus; the index is 315 MB today. Nobody has priced it — that measurement is the first task if this is taken up.

## Why it is filed as a decision

It changes the index schema and needs an IMPORTER_VERSION bump and a reindex, and ADR 6's 'revisit when' now names it. It is also the only remaining lever on the two queries chat-search-6eb.30 could not get under the 30 ms keystroke budget, because after that change the marking is 6-12 ms of them and the ranking is the other 29-59 ms.
design: Measure first, decide second. The sequence: build the index with prefix='2 3', with prefix='2 3 4', and without; record file size and rebuild time for each; re-run the search_grouped numbers in chat-search-6eb.29 and the per-row marking numbers in highlight::spans_for against all three. If a prefix index makes the index route cheap for prefix terms too, highlight::spans_for's two-branch rule collapses back to one branch, which is a second reason to want it.
acceptance_criteria: Either the fts tables declare a prefix index, with the size cost measured and recorded in ADR 6 and IMPORTER_VERSION bumped — or the option is measured, rejected, and the rejection written down so it is not re-litigated.

title: cs-tui reads the query mode instead of re-deriving it
description:
Delete App::holds, App::holding, App::is_blank and state::MIN_QUERY_CHARS. The TUI reads Query::mode and decides what to render for each of Empty, TooShort and Searchable.

Also deletes SearchOptions.source from the TUI path: the facet selection desugars into Filter::Agent. Surfaces dir: and date: as recognised-but-not-yet-active in the status line, which is the chat-search-me9.15 gap.

Removes the reason App::holds was lifted out as a pure associated function in the first place, so its index-free test moves to cs-core with the rule.
close_reason: Closed

title: Rank and mark from the parsed query
description:
Migrate search.rs and highlight.rs to render from one structure, and delete the six exported tokenizing functions plus highlight::query_terms. snippet_marked survives with a new signature. highlight::spans and highlight::snippet are untouched: the fts5 scratch-table mechanism from chat-search-6eb.20 is correct and is not what leaks.

Wire Filter::Agent to the source clause that already exists (AND (?4 IS NULL OR c.source = ?4)), and carry dir:/date: as recognised-but-inactive.

Tests: one structural invariant asserting match_expr and marking_terms render from the same term list, plus the three divergences as named regression cases on search.rs:456. That table currently calls highlight::query_terms directly and never sets prefix, so the test written to pin agreement cannot catch the bugs it exists to prevent. Route it through Query::typeahead and marking_terms, the path that actually ships.
close_reason: Closed

title: New cs-core/src/query.rs: parse, Query, Filter, Mode
description:
The parsed value and its tests, with no callers yet.

Query::typeahead(text) and Query::exact(text) fix prefix at parse time. Query carries ordered terms, filters, whether the final token is still open, and Mode { Empty, TooShort, Searchable }. Parse is infallible: a half-typed filter is literal text, never an error, because mid-word is the normal state in a typeahead.

Also adds the terms to docs/GLOSSARY.md, which today has no word for any of this. The glossary opens with the story of a wrong name propagating through a spec and two implementations before the data contradicted it, so the terms land with the type rather than after it.
close_reason: Closed

title: Split SearchOptions out of Query, and require now_ms
description:
cs_core::search::Query holds two concepts: what the user asked for (text) and how to run it (limit, field, source, include_off_path, prefix, now_ms, repeat_weight, decay). That conflation is why recent() accepts a Query and silently ignores seven of its nine fields.

Rename the bag to SearchOptions so the name Query is free for the parsed value. Fold the positional nested argument of search_grouped into it while there.

Make now_ms a required argument to SearchOptions::new rather than a defaultable field. Query::new leaves it 0, and the decay term is bm25 / (1.0 + decay * max(0, now_ms - ts) / YEAR): with now_ms = 0 and any positive timestamp, max(0, 0 - ts) is 0, so the divisor is exactly 1.0 and recency decay is silently off. Fixes the explain bug in the same move.

Must land before the new Query type: both would otherwise be re-exported from lib.rs as Query.
close_reason: Closed

title: Rename cs/src/query.rs to commands.rs
description: crates/cs/src/query.rs is named for query parsing and contains none. Its own module doc says what it holds: cs index, cs search and cs explain, everything downstream of the archive. Adding a real crates/cs-core/src/query.rs would put two files named query.rs in the workspace, only one of which parses queries. Mechanical: one mod line, one import line, no logic touched.
close_reason: Closed

title: Parse the query once, into a value
description:
The query is a &str re-tokenized on every path. search::to_match_expr_opts and highlight::query_terms are two term extractors with different rules, bridged by marking_terms, which recovers the prefix rule by string-inspecting the ranker output (expr.ends_with). App::holds re-derives the same MIN_PREFIX_LEN threshold as its logical complement, and is_blank asks a third time.

TWO live divergences, measured 2026-07-30 by probing both extractors directly:

  agent:codex borrow  expr="agent" "codex" "borrow"*   marking=["borrow*"]
  learn deep learn    expr="learn" "deep" "learn"*     marking=["learn", "deep"]

1. agent:codex is ANDed into FTS5 as two literal terms while the highlighter drops them, so every returned row is labelled with the UNLOCATED sentinel. The highlight.rs comment claiming the row was not ranked on those words is false today.
2. learn deep learn loses its prefix star. query_terms deduplicates, so terms.last() is deep while the expression ends with "learn"*, the ends_with check misses, and a row that ranked on the stem expansion is marked with the exact term or not at all.

CORRECTION: an earlier draft listed a third divergence, -borrow becoming a required term. Probed: both sides produce "borrow"* and they agree. Leading-dash negation is simply unimplemented, which is a chat-search-6eb.11 feature gap rather than a defect here. Two divergences, not three.

Fix: parse once into a Query value that both the ranker and the highlighter render from. Not a harder ends_with check, no bridge at all.
design:
Decided by grilling, 2026-07-30. Eleven decisions:

1. Seam only. Filter tokens are recognised so they stop reaching FTS5 as literal words. The DSL itself stays chat-search-6eb.11.
2. Two types. Query is what was asked (terms, filters, open, mode). SearchOptions is how to run it (limit, field, decay, repeat_weight, now_ms, nested). The conflation is why recent() silently ignores seven of nine fields.
3. Mode { Empty, TooShort, Searchable } lives on Query. cs-core owns the fact (the threshold is a ranking cost: h* 2510ms, ho* 51ms, hov* 16ms), cs-tui owns the policy.
4. A filter that cannot be applied is recognised, carried and surfaced, never silently dropped. Serves chat-search-me9.15.
5. Full absorption. Query::typeahead and Query::exact fix prefix at PARSE time, not render time. Prefix-agnostic parse was considered and rejected: Mode::TooShort exists only because of prefix expansion, so mode(), match_expr() and marking_terms() would each take the same bool and have to be passed it consistently, which is the bug class being removed.
6. One internal home for filters. --source and facet clicks desugar into Query.filters at the edge. TUI-DESIGN section 5: fast-resume kept a second source of truth and paid six reconciliation methods.
7. agent: goes live, dir: and date: are surfaced-inactive. The source clause already exists as AND (?4 IS NULL OR c.source = ?4), so Filter::Agent feeds ?4 rather than adding a clause. Without this, deleting SearchOptions.source would silently break --source and the facet bar.
8. New crates/cs-core/src/query.rs. crates/cs/src/query.rs is renamed to commands.rs, since it holds command handlers and no parser.
9. now_ms becomes a required argument to SearchOptions::new. The 0 default silently disables decay.
10. Structural invariant test plus regression table, routed through Query::typeahead and marking_terms rather than query_terms.
11. Five commits, each green.

Parse is infallible, per chat-search-6eb.11 acceptance criteria: a half-typed filter is literal text, never an error.

Deleted: to_match_expr, to_match_expr_opts, snippet, snippet_opts, marking_terms, is_blank, highlight::query_terms, App::holds, App::holding, App::is_blank, state::MIN_QUERY_CHARS, SearchOptions.source. snippet_marked survives with a new signature. highlight::spans and highlight::snippet are untouched, the 6eb.20 scratch-table mechanism is correct.
acceptance_criteria: agent:codex borrow ranks on borrow alone and filters to source=codex. -borrow is not a required term. learn deep learn keeps its prefix star. dir: and date: are carried and surfaced as not-yet-active rather than silently ignored. One structural test asserts match_expr and marking_terms render from the same term list. cargo test --workspace green at every one of the five commits, and cargo build --workspace --all-targets warning-free.
close_reason: Closed

title: Cache the preview layout between frames so scrolling stops rebuilding it
description:
Preview::layout does not depend on scroll, yet every frame rebuilt every row of the conversation to move the viewport a few lines. Measured on the corpus longest conversation: 38.9 ms to lay out 9,261 rows at width 96, of which ~85% is wrapping (6.1 ms at a width nothing can exceed) and 0% is mark-splitting (38.9 with marks vs 38.7 with none). None of that changes as the pane scrolls.

Rows are now cached behind an Rc, keyed on (width, focus, generation). scroll is deliberately absent from the key - that is the entire saving. focus is present because it styles the focused chevron; generation is bumped by every fold and density change. Keyed rather than eagerly cleared so a resize or a fold can never be served rows measured for a different pane.

MEASURED AFTER (same conversation, width 96, 9,261 rows):
  layout, scroll-only frame : 0.0000 ms  (was 38.9 ms)
  layout, cold after a fold : 51 ms      (unchanged - see me9.1.1.11)
  lines() clone for Paragraph: 0.65 ms   (cheap; no borrow rework needed)
Stress harness of 168,000 scroll notches across 7 pane sizes: 67 s -> 17.6 s.

Also checked what ratatui could take over, and it cannot. Paragraph already stops painting at area.height, which is why drawing is only 1.6 ms. Paragraph::wrap(Wrap) would do the wrapping, but with wrap enabled its scroll is O(scroll offset) per frame - paragraph.rs runs next_line() scroll.y times to skip - and it will not report where it broke, so the row-to-message map that clicks and follow_focus need would be lost.
acceptance_criteria: A scroll-only frame reuses the same rows by identity; width, focus, folds and density each rebuild them.
close_reason: Landed 2026-07-30. Scroll-only frames went 38.9 ms -> 0.0000 ms; the stress harness of 168,000 notches across 7 pane sizes went 67 s -> 17.6 s. 364 tests passing, zero warnings.

title: Preview lays out the whole conversation every frame; 43ms on the largest
description:
Separate from me9.1.1.6, which is the one-time open cost. This is per-frame.

render::preview calls p.lines() -> Preview::layout() on every draw, and layout walks the entire conversation building styled, wrapped rows for all of it - then Paragraph::scroll throws away everything outside the viewport. Measured on the largest conversation (1,468 blocks, 942 KB, width 96): 43.4 ms to produce 9,261 rows, of which about 35 are on screen. Painting the frame is 1.6 ms, so essentially all of it is layout.

That is paid on every keystroke and every scroll burst, and on its own it exceeds the 30 ms budget for a conversation of that size. The scroll-burst coalescing in me9.1.1.10 reduced how OFTEN it is paid but not what it costs.

Note the height memoisation added in me9.1.1.10 does not help here: it caches the row COUNT for the scroll clamp, while rendering still needs the rows themselves.
design: Lay out only the visible window. layout() would take (scroll, viewport_rows) and skip blocks whose height puts them off screen - but block heights are exactly what layout computes, so it needs a cheap height pass or a per-block height cache to skip ahead without building rows. Note that block_at_row and follow_focus also read layout(), so whatever shape this takes must keep them reading the same geometry - that single-source property is what me9.1.1.9 established and it must not be traded away for speed.
acceptance_criteria: A frame of the largest conversation lays out in well under the 30ms budget; clicks and scrolling still resolve to the same rows the renderer drew.
notes:
NARROWED by me9.1.1.12 (layout caching), which landed 2026-07-30. Scroll-only frames are now free, so this is no longer a per-frame cost on the hot path.

What remains is the COLD path: the first layout after a fold, a density change, a resize, or selecting a new conversation still builds every row. Measured 51 ms on the corpus longest conversation (9,261 rows at width 96), and ~85% of that is wrapping rows that are never on screen.

Windowing is still the fix and the constraint is unchanged - block_at_row and follow_focus read the same layout, and that single-source property must survive. The cache makes it easier: per-block heights can live beside the cached rows rather than being recomputed to skip ahead.
close_reason:
Closed 2026-07-30 without windowing the layout, which measurement said was the wrong fix.

The 51 ms was not the breadth of the work but a quadratic loop inside it: prefix_end re-measured the whole prefix for every character, ~w²/2 width lookups per row, ~42M over the 9,261 rows of the longest conversation. A printable-ASCII fast path takes layout to 22.6 ms. Selecting that conversation - load, marking and first frame - is now 82 ms against 240 ms before this and the batching in me9.1.1.6; a scroll frame is 2.9 ms p50; the stress harness of 168,000 notches is 4.2 s against 67 s at the start.

Windowing was prototyped far enough to price it. A height-only pass measured 65% of a full layout before the fix and ~43% after, so it would now save ~13 ms on the cold path only, and it would cost the single-source-of-geometry property: block_at_row and follow_focus reading a height derived separately from the rows drawn is exactly the arrangement that put clicks on the wrong message. Not worth it. The scaffolding (text::wrapped_rows) was removed rather than left as unused API.

Reopen if the cold path matters again - the note above records where the remaining time is (SQL read and hydration, ~44 ms).

title: claude-desktop importer for local-agent-mode sessions
description:
Claude Desktop's Cowork and Chat tabs write full transcripts to disk in the clear, and nothing reads them. Surveyed 2026-07-30: ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/local-agent-mode-sessions/<account>/<org>/ holds 14 sessions, 30 MB, 736 assistant + 598 user messages. This is the only dark surface that needs no export, no API, no browser and no credentials — it is the cheapest coverage in the Capture epic.

Earlier notes concluded 'Claude desktop needs export or API' after inspecting IndexedDB alone. That part is right (it is a React Query cache, zero message bodies) but the conclusion was drawn from the wrong directory.

Format detail in docs/FORMAT-NOTES.md, section 'Claude desktop - local agent mode'.
design:
New source id 'claude-desktop' (permanent, ADR 16). Distinct from 'claude-ai', which theme.rs already reserves for the cloud-synced conversations this does NOT cover.

Wiring is the standard five touches: SOURCE const + import fn in crates/cs-import/src/claude_desktop.rs, pub mod in lib.rs, a match arm in crates/cs/src/query.rs::import_source, a detect_sources() candidate in crates/cs-archive/src/config.rs, and a KNOWN_SOURCES entry in crates/cs-tui/src/theme.rs.

Three traps, all measured:
1. The transcript is local_<uuid>/audit.jsonl but title/model/cwd/timestamps live in the SIBLING local_<uuid>.json. Neither is sufficient alone. The importer is a pure fn over (logical_path, bytes), so it cannot read the sibling - either the glob covers both and a second pass folds them on the uuid in the logical path, or titles come from initialMessage in-band. Prefer the fold; it matches how Codex folds threads on session_id.
2. Shape is Agent SDK stream-json, NOT Claude Code JSONL. snake_case session_id/parent_tool_use_id vs camelCase sessionId/parentUuid. Close enough to invite widening the claude-code glob, different enough that doing so imports zero.
3. parent_tool_use_id is not a message parent - it marks subagent messages under a tool call. Feeding it to parent_native_id breaks index::on_head_path, which requires a parent the importer actually emitted. The file is linear; leave parent_native_id as the previous emitted message.

Only 14 of 165 JSON files here are conversation-bearing. Decline by shape the way gemini.rs declines logs.json, not by trusting the glob.
acceptance_criteria: cs index reports a claude-desktop row with a non-zero conversation count against the real archive. Sessions carry a title (not a uuid) and a model. A session directory with no audit.jsonl is skipped without an error. Widening the claude-code glob to these files is shown by test to import zero, so the two importers cannot be collapsed by a later reader.
close_reason:
Implemented and verified end to end against the real archive on 2026-07-30: 106 archived files -> 14 conversations, 1,200 messages, 203 prose, 0 off-head-path. Titles and models land from the state file, timestamps from the audit clock, and cs search returns them under a claude.app badge.

Three findings worth carrying forward, all recorded in docs/FORMAT-NOTES.md:
- A transcript carries TWO session ids and the one matching the directory is the minority holder (19 records vs 405 for the CLI session underneath). Keying on either splits the conversation, so the importer keys on the local_<uuid> path segment.
- Repeated uuids are almost entirely isReplay turns re-emitted on resume, not corruption.
- The acceptance criterion 'widening the claude-code glob imports zero' was WRONG and the test now pins the truth: claude_code::import already accepts both sessionId and session_id, so it parses these files happily and files them under the wrong source with a claude --resume command that cannot reopen a desktop session, and without titles. The failure looks like success, which is the reason to keep two importers.

title: Preview scroll ran to u16::MAX past the end and rebuilt the layout per notch
description:
Reported: scrolling the preview too far makes it "freak out" and the program crashes, leaving a flood of raw SGR mouse reports in the terminal.

Could NOT reproduce a panic. A stress harness drove 168,000 scroll notches to u16 saturation and back across 7 pane sizes (140x40, 116x40, 115x40, 60x12, 20x6, 8x4, 400x100) over 25 conversations of the real index, redrawing through TestBackend and click-mapping every row at each step: no crash. The leaked escape sequences are unread mouse reports still in the tty buffer being echoed by the shell once the app exited, so they say the app went away mid-gesture, not where.

Three real defects found and fixed on the way, two of which fully explain the "freaks out":

1. SCROLL WAS UNBOUNDED. scroll_preview did a saturating_add with no ceiling, so scrolling past the last line kept counting to 65535. The pane went blank with nothing to say how far past the end it was, and getting back meant winding the same distance in reverse. Now clamped to the last screenful via Preview::scroll_by.

2. SCROLLING WAS O(CONVERSATION) PER NOTCH. The clamp needs the rendered height, and laying the whole pane out per notch made a trackpad flick quadratic in conversation length. Memoised on Preview, keyed by width, dropped by every edit that changes what is drawn. The stress run went from >600s to 67s for the same events.

3. ONE UNREADABLE EVENT KILLED THE SESSION. event::read()? sent any error straight out of event_loop, so a single transient parse or I/O failure during a fast scroll threw away the query and tore the session down - which matches the report exactly. Now tolerates up to MAX_MISREADS consecutive failures; a persistently unreadable stream still stops.

Also: the loop redrew once per event, so a flick of hundreds of reports meant hundreds of full renders and the pane crawled behind the finger. It now absorbs a burst of up to BURST queued events into one frame.
acceptance_criteria: Scrolling stops at the end of the conversation and one notch back up is one notch; folding invalidates the cached height; a transient input error does not end the session.
close_reason: Landed 2026-07-30. Fenced blocks render dim behind a two-column rule (section 8 treatment, no dependency; syntect measured at +2.1MB and ~110us/line to colour the 3.9% of prose messages that tag a language). Match highlight takes Color::Blue from the indexed palette - index 4 is the slot Solarized fills with #268BD2, so a Solarized terminal gets that exact hue and every other terminal inherits its own; DIM is subtracted so a match never recedes inside dim snippet or code text. Preview body text now wraps at word boundaries instead of truncating, which forced the real fix: Preview::layout is the single source of geometry, returning each drawn row paired with the message that put it there, so what is drawn, what a click resolves to and what scrolling counts cannot drift. Scroll is clamped to the last screenful, its height memoised per width and invalidated on every fold, and the event loop absorbs an input burst into one frame and survives a transient unreadable event instead of ending the session. Verified against the real 2,980-conversation index and a 168,000-notch stress harness across 7 pane sizes. 363 tests passing (317 at the start of this work), zero warnings.

title: Wrap preview body text instead of truncating each line to the pane
description:
Requested: wrap text in the preview window instead of showing one line and truncating. Long prose is currently unreadable - every source line is cut at the pane width.

Not a rendering-only change. Preview::rendered_rows computed a message height as 2 + line count, which only held while one source line was exactly one terminal row; the click map and follow_focus both counted with it. Wrapping ends that, and a second derivation of the same geometry would drift the moment a line wrapped - invisibly, until a click folded the wrong message. The old block_at_row comment called this out as the hazard.

Fixed structurally: Preview::layout is now the single source of geometry, returning each drawn row paired with the message that put it there. lines(), block_at_row() and follow_focus() all read it, so what is drawn, what a click resolves to and what scrolling counts cannot disagree. Callers pass the pane inner width via render::preview_body_width, because resolving a click at any other width wraps differently and counts a row that is not on screen.
acceptance_criteria: A long paragraph occupies several rows and every one resolves to its own message; a narrow pane needs more rows than a wide one; the gutter rule repeats down every wrapped row of a fenced block.
close_reason: Landed 2026-07-30. title: Collapsed prose shows the matching line, and the preview anchors on the best hit
description:
Two halves of the same idea: put the reason the row is here in front of the user without making them scroll.

MATCHING LINE. Section 8 specs collapsed prose as 'role sigil + the MATCHING line, else the first non-empty line'. preview.rs:304 first_line() always takes the first non-empty. This is the whole reason section 8 argues outline mode beats a density knob — 'you see every place the query hit, across the whole conversation, in conversation order'. Today outline mode is a table of contents, not a match map.

ANCHORING. Preview::load hardcodes focus: 0, scroll: 0, so selecting a result always opens at message 1 rather than the message that matched.

TRAP: do NOT anchor on g.hits[0]. state.rs:123 runs search_grouped(.., 0) — no snippets per keystroke — so hits are empty until the row is expanded with Tab, and anchoring would silently work only on expanded rows. Anchor on Group::match_seqs (search.rs:526), which IS populated at nested=0; it already drives the density strip.

title: Preview highlights message bodies; marks computed once per message, never per line
description:
preview.rs:222-225 defers highlighting to 6eb.20, which is now CLOSED — the blocker is gone. Preview::lines() does not take the query terms yet.
